newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria, EU to discuss association deal on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Algeria, EU to discuss association deal on Tuesday.

text.p: Negotiations between Algeria and the European Union on an association accord will begin on Tuesday, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Monday.
Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia held a last meeting on Sunday with about 20 Algerian negotiators, headed by diplomat Mohamed Lamari, Algerian state-run television said.
Algerian officials have said the accord they want with the 15-nation European bloc would be similar to deals linking the European Union to Israel, Tunisia and Morocco.
Algeria began preliminary talks with the European Union in June 1994, with the latest meeting last month, officials said.
The European Commission got permission last June to negotiate the deal with Algeria -- offering financial, social and cultural links -- to replace a pact that has been in place since 1978.
The accord envisages an eventual free trade zone with the European Union.
Algerian President Liamine Zeroual last April ordered the government to press ahead with talks on the trade accord, saying it would have a huge impact on the economy.
Algeria has been battered by civil strife since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
About 60,000 people have died in the five years of violence in the North Afrian country, which provides much of Europe's energy needs through its oil and gas exports.
